expectations_used.clarify: Establishes how duplicate values and reused indices behave in findPairs before designing.
expectations_used.approach: States the algorithm and its complexity — e.g. a hashmap pass making it O(n) versus the naive O(n^2) — BEFORE writing code.
expectations_used.communicate: Talks through the pair-collection logic while implementing it.
expectations_used.implement: Implementation follows the stated algorithm for collecting unique index pairs.
expectations_used.verify: Dry-runs findPairs on an example with duplicates and re-runs the suite including the large-input test.
expectations_used.reflect: Restates the complexity and where the hashmap approach would break.

summary: The candidate iterated from a brute-force O(n^2) solution to a hashmap-based O(n) approach after correctly diagnosing a timeout on the large-input test, verified the fix with a manual dry run and a full green test run, and clearly narrated their reasoning throughout. This is a clean, well-communicated build-round session with strong process across nearly every dimension.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate did not ask clarifying questions upfront, but before committing to the dedup logic, they checked the test file to confirm how duplicates and index reuse should behave, resolving the ambiguity themselves rather than guessing blind. This was a bit late (after already writing a brute force pass) but it was a real self-directed check of the spec before finalizing logic.

After the brute force solution timed out on the large input, the candidate explicitly diagnosed the O(n^2) mechanism as the cause, then stated a concrete hashmap-based O(n) algorithm — storing value-to-indices and checking for the complement — before writing any code for it. This is a mechanism-level plan, not just a vague location or intent.

The candidate narrated their thinking almost continuously: describing the brute force loop before writing it, flagging the complexity concern, stating the hashmap plan, and then narrating a full dry run step by step with concrete values. The transcript alone makes their path easy to follow.

Implementation tracked the stated plans at each stage: brute force loop matched the stated pseudocode, and the rewrite matched the stated hashmap approach. When a bug surfaced (complement-equals-self edge case), they diagnosed it precisely and fixed the check-before-insert ordering rather than thrashing.

Before even running the suite the final time, the candidate manually dry-ran the hashmap algorithm against a concrete example with duplicate values, tracing index-by-index behavior, and only then reran the full test suite including the large-input case to confirm the fix.

At the end the candidate restated the complexity characteristics of the final solution (O(n) time and space) and earlier had already articulated why the initial approach failed and why the map ordering bug occurred, connecting cause to fix rather than treating the green run as magic.
